value.quote:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$ be a unital $R$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), with $A$ regarded as its left regular module.

1. For $a,b\in A$ one has $a=b$ if and only if $a\cdot1_A=b\cdot1_A$.
2. For $n\ge1$ the tensor power $A^{\otimes n}$ is a left $A$-module via $a\cdot(a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n)=(aa_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$. If $a\cdot z=b\cdot z$ for all $z\in A^{\otimes n}$, then $a=b$; in particular the single element $1_A^{\otimes n}$ detects equality. The analogous statement holds for the right regular structure. The empty tensor power $A^{\otimes0}=R$ carries no canonical left $A$-module structure here, so no $n=0$ case is claimed.
3. For $n\ge1$, if $f,g:A^{\times n}\to M$ are $R$-multilinear and agree on every $n$-tuple, then the $R$-linear maps $A^{\otimes n}\to M$ they induce ([[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]) agree; conversely, agreement of the induced maps gives agreement on all pure tensors $a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$.
4. Descent warning: if $\pi:A\to A/I$ is a quotient of $R$-algebras ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]), the induced map $A^{\otimes n}\to(A/I)^{\otimes n}$ is surjective, but an identity between $R$-linear maps out of $(A/I)^{\otimes n}$ may be checked on images of pure tensors of $A$ only after those maps have been shown to be well defined on the quotient; surjectivity alone is not descent.

value: For the converse, apply the assumed tensor-module law to the regular left modules $H,H$. The action of $h$ on $1_H\otimes1_H$ is $\Delta(h)$. Associativity of the action gives $\Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\Delta(b)$ after evaluating at $1_H\otimes1_H$; [F8] justifies that this regular tensor vector detects equality in $H\otimes H$. The unital action law similarly gives $\Delta(1_H)=1_H\otimes1_H$. Thus $\Delta$ is a unital algebra map.

For the converse, use the regular left modules $H,H$. The action formula gives $b\cdot(1_H\otimes1_H)=\Delta(b)$ and $(ab)\cdot(1_H\otimes1_H)=\Delta(ab)$. By the assumed associativity of this tensor-module action, $\Delta(ab)=(ab)\cdot(1_H\otimes1_H)=a\cdot\bigl(b\cdot(1_H\otimes1_H)\bigr)=a\cdot\Delta(b)=\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\Delta(a)\Delta(b)$, where the last equality uses the tensor-product algebra multiplication [F3]. The assumed unital action law gives $1_H\otimes1_H=1_H\cdot(1_H\otimes1_H)=\Delta(1_H)$. Thus $\Delta$ is a unital algebra map.

Apply $H$-linearity of the canonical associator to the three regular modules and evaluate at $1_H\otimes1_H\otimes1_H$. The action on the left-parenthesized tensor gives $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(h)$ there, while the right-parenthesized tensor gives $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta(h)$. Their equality follows from $H$-linearity, and [F8] says this tensor detects equality; hence $\Delta$ is coassociative.

Apply $H$-linearity of the canonical associator to the three regular modules at $((1_H\otimes1_H)\otimes1_H)$. The action on this left-parenthesized unit tensor is $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(h)$, and applying the associator sends it to $\alpha((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(h))$ in $H\otimes(H\otimes H)$. On the right-parenthesized unit tensor, the action is $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta(h)$. Since the associator sends the unit tensor to the right-parenthesized unit tensor, its $H$-linearity gives $\alpha((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(h))=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta(h)$, precisely coassociativity with the canonical associator [F6].
